clue.text: Loyal support? Alas, I scam everyone

indicators.note: a cry of dismay suggests things have gone wrong, so the following letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A con artist laments that he swindles every person he meets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alas' looks like an interjection lamenting the scam but signals an anagram of I SCAM EVERYONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means faithful, dependable help, from the reliability of the old English small landowners who served as soldiers.

clue.text: Scope to jog over cell

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: to jog someone is to nudge them, as with an elbow
a cell is a small room

explanation.surface: A prisoner wonders whether there is space to go running over the cell.
explanation.definitionFit: Space to move freely is scope or latitude.

clue.text: Relating to large masses may be called wisdom

definitions.meaning: in physics and chemistry the adjective describes bulk mass as opposed to molecules
a wisdom tooth is a kind of back grinding tooth

explanation.surface: Something weighty might be deemed wise.
explanation.definitionFit: A grinding back tooth includes the wisdom teeth; the adjective in physics concerns bodies of mass.

clue.text: Is the rest of the head straight in this bunch?

definitions.text: Is the rest of the head straight in this bunch?

parts.words: Is the rest of the head straight in this bunch?
parts.note: the part of the head between eyes and mouth followed by a word meaning not straight answers the question; the whole is a small bunch of flowers

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about whether the rest of someone's head is straight.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into the facial feature and a word meaning not heterosexual: the question asks if that feature is straight, and the answer says it is not.
explanation.definitionFit: A small posy of sweet-smelling flowers is a small bunch, often carried.

clue.text: Old lawman to carry personal protection

parts.note: Wyatt Earp was a famous lawman of the American Wild West
to lug is to carry something heavy

explanation.surface: A Wild West marshal carries something to protect himself, presumably a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a firearm; the protection is for the ears against noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug worn in the ear guards hearing, a piece of personal protective equipment.

clue.text: Reveals it to be flexible

indicators.note: the letters of the first words are shown 'to be', i.e. transformed into, the definition word, signalling rearrangement

explanation.surface: A test shows that something turns out to be bendy.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of REVEALS IT rearrange into the answer; 'to be' is the thin signal that they become something else.
explanation.definitionFit: Being adaptable to many uses or roles is being flexible.

clue.text: Rope caught by type of seaman

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an able seaman is a rank in the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A sailor of some rank catches hold of a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick heavy rope or wire, as used to moor a ship, is this.

clue.text: A particular dark time to sustain a casual relationship

parts.note: a single specific night is a particular dark time
to stand something is to bear or sustain it

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether one bleak evening can keep a fling going.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief sexual encounter lasting a single evening is a casual liaison.

clue.text: Arrogant greeting good worker could eventually deny

parts.note: hi is a greeting
a hand is a manual worker
might is a past form meaning could

indicators.note: eventually points to the end, so the last letter of deny is taken

explanation.surface: A haughty boss's hello to a decent employee might in time be refused.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaving with self-important superiority over others is being haughty or arrogant.

clue.text: Spray blue rinse all over the place

indicators.note: letters scattered all over the place are disordered, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A hairdresser's tint spray ends up everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A device turning liquid medicine into a fine mist for inhaling produces a spray.

clue.text: Book ban rescinded by one leader of congregation

indicators.note: something rescinded is turned back, so the word for ban is reversed

parts.note: to bar is to ban
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A clergyman revokes a ban on a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish religious teacher typically leads a synagogue's congregation.

clue.text: Never has waist doubled? Not that old!

indicators.note: the waist of the word is its middle letter, a V; doubling a V gives a double-u, so that letter is swapped

explanation.surface: A vain person insists their waistline has never grown twice as large, protesting they are not old.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter V of NEVER becomes W, which looks like two Vs side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Something more recent than another is not as old, a comparative of fresh.

clue.text: Man impressed to have left sport, quiet epic hero

parts.note: an impressed man is one pressed into military service, and GI is an American conscript soldier
a game is a sport
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A conscript who has quit sport is impressed by a silent epic hero.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sumerian king is the protagonist of the ancient Mesopotamian epic poem bearing his name.

clue.text: Bad-tempered Greek that hurt you early on

parts.note: ouch is the cry meaning that hurt

indicators.note: early on points to the start, so the first letter of you is taken

explanation.surface: A grumpy Greek complains that you hurt him early on.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumbling and irritable is a synonym for bad-tempered.

clue.text: Join in as craftsman took a meal

parts.note: a cooper is a craftsman who makes barrels
ate means took a meal

explanation.surface: An artisan joins a group as it sits down to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: To work together with others is to participate or join in.

clue.text: Shine, having first to break depression

indicators.note: one piece breaks into the other, going inside it

parts.note: a glen is a valley, a depression in land
1ST, written as IST, is short for first

explanation.surface: A glow emerges having first broken through a low mood.
explanation.definitionFit: To sparkle or gleam, especially of wet surfaces, is to shine.

clue.text: Miniaturised state introduces new poor quality of sound reproduction

indicators.note: the state introduces a letter, taking it inside

parts.note: tininess is the state of being very small

explanation.surface: Shrinking hi-fi gear brings in a new tinny sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, metallic, cheap-sounding audio quality is the hallmark of poor sound reproduction.

clue.text: Male caught in snare unconscious, going to expire

indicators.note: the letter is caught inside the snare

parts.note: to tie is to bind or ensnare
someone out cold is unconscious

explanation.surface: A man trapped and knocked out is about to die.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests death; a session that will expire is one that will time out.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer session that runs out of allowed time is said to expire, i.e. stop.

clue.text: What may make one warm?

parts.note: a playful hint: the action of melting from frozen makes something warm again, and WHAT plus a word for out reads hidden in the solution

explanation.surface: A simple question about what warms a person up.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word of the clue appears, letters rearranged, as the first word of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfreeze, as frozen food or a chilled person does, is to become warm.

clue.text: Bone is hard? I'm pondering

parts.note: stern means hard or severe
um is the sound of someone thinking

explanation.surface: Someone muses on whether a bone is hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat breastbone in the chest is a bone.

clue.text: Wait in court, present at table

parts.note: to serve is to wait at table
a defendant up before the judge is in court

explanation.surface: A tennis player waits in court, or a waiter brings out food.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring food out and dish it to diners is to present it at table.

clue.text: Equitable dealings out of order in this business meeting

indicators.note: the two words of the phrase equitable dealings are taken in the opposite order

parts.note: trade is commercial dealings
fair means equitable

explanation.surface: Ethical commerce is unwelcome at a commercial gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: Equitable dealings is FAIR TRADE; 'out of order' swaps the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhibition where companies show goods to buyers is a business meeting.

clue.text: Hearing defective behind area in courtyards

indicators.note: the shortened hearing comes behind, after, the area letter
defective means lacking a part, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing

explanation.surface: A faulty hearing aid is found behind some courtyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Open central halls or courts in Roman houses, plural of the Latin word, are courtyards.

clue.text: Man of note fell a minute short, say

indicators.note: the word is left short of a letter, which is removed

parts.note: as an adjective fell means grim or cruel
M is an abbreviation for minute
eg, for example, means say

explanation.surface: Someone toppled a minute too soon, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like a verb but is the adjective meaning cruel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian composer was a celebrated musician, a man of musical notes.

clue.text: Father and Son: son goes off to be an author

indicators.note: off means wrong or bad, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: In a family drama, the son leaves to become a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Father and Son is the memoir by Edmund Gosse, linking the surface to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Gosse was a Victorian English poet, critic and writer.

clue.text: Woman not entirely like the others?

indicators.note: not entirely means one letter is missing from the end

parts.note: normal means like the others, conventional

explanation.surface: A woman who is somewhat different from everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, as in the opera heroine, stands for a woman.

clue.text: Not to one's taste and bad for one: two severe blows

definitions.text: Not to one's taste and bad for one

indicators.note: letters that blow about are scattered, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Something disagreeable and harmful arrives as two hard punches.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessively sugary food is unpleasant to many palates and unhealthy.

clue.text: So enthusiastic, corruptly agree best contract

indicators.note: corruptly means in a twisted way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: top means best
a lease is a rental contract

explanation.surface: A keen party corruptly consents to the most favourable deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Highly keen to satisfy or oblige others describes an enthusiastic, obliging person.
